question: to the Commission Ondřej Dostál (NI) Subject:

Since the end of the COVID-19 pandemic, the regular meetings of the EU-India Joint Working Group on Pharmaceuticals, Biotechnology and Medical Devices have been suspended. What is the reason for this suspension?

India, a country with traditional strengths in the pharmaceutical and medical sectors, could help protect EU citizens in the event of a future pandemic through the export of medicines and vaccines. Why are the Indian authorities’ requests for a meeting going unanswered?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (13.7.2026) The Commission recognises India’s importance in global pharmaceutical supply chains, which helps ensuring access to affordable, safe, and effective medicines – a priority for EU citizens. Meetings of the EU-India Joint Working Group on Pharmaceuticals, Biotechnology, and Medical Devices were regularly held until 2020, with discussions covering regulatory alignment, supply chain resilience, and innovation. No further meetings took place during the EU-India Free Trade Agreement (FTA) negotiations, because these negotiations included discussions on pharmaceutical and health-related provisions. With the FTA now concluded, the Commission is further assessing the most effective format to engage with India.
